statement: How many three-digit numbers have all three digits different and do not contain a zero?

choices.misconception: I allowed digits to repeat, using nine choices in every one of the three places.
I used ten digits for the first place, although zero is excluded throughout.
I allowed a zero in the last two places, which the question forbids.
I excluded one digit too many, leaving eight choices for every place.

hints: Count the choices for each place in turn.
Fill the places one at a time. Nine digits are available for the first, then one fewer for each later place, because digits may not repeat and zero is excluded throughout.
Nine choices, then eight, then seven.

solutions.reliable: Zero is excluded, so nine digits are available. The first place has 9 choices, the second 8 and the third 7, giving 9 x 8 x 7 = 504. The transferable idea: handle the restriction by shrinking the pool before counting, then let each placement reduce the count by one.

whyOnTest: Restricted counting goes wrong when repeats slip back in, and the unrestricted counts are all offered.
